messages:
evan-support: FYI customer reported being charged $120 after a subscription swap that should have generated a prorate credit. Customer: cus_ABC123. Need rollback and root cause.

tool-router-bot: Incident created: INC-4321 :rotating_light: — automated alert: abnormal billing event detected for cus_ABC123.

ashley-cs: Can you paste the API call and the transaction id? I'll pull the invoice.

evan-support: Repro request + API call below. Transaction id is tx_9XyZ.
```json
POST /v1/subscriptions/swap
{
  "customer_id": "cus_ABC123",
  "from_plan": "startup-monthly",
  "to_plan": "pro-monthly",
  "effective_date": "2026-03-10",
  "prorate": true
}
```

matt-eng: Pasting trimmed router logs — looks like the tool resolver picked billing.create_charge instead of billing.create_prorate_credit.
```
[2026-03-10T15:12:01Z] [tool-router] input_tokens=34 intent="subscription.swap" aliases_matched=["prorate","swap"]
[2026-03-10T15:12:01Z] [tool-router] candidates=["billing.create_charge","billing.create_prorate_credit"]
[2026-03-10T15:12:01Z] [tool-router] scoring={"billing.create_charge":0.67,"billing.create_prorate_credit":0.63} // weight bias: usage_prior=+0.05
[2026-03-10T15:12:01Z] [tool-router] selected="billing.create_charge"
[2026-03-10T15:12:01Z] [tool-exec] args={"customer_id":"cus_ABC123","amount_cents":12000,"reason":"proration"}
[2026-03-10T15:12:02Z] [billing-service] charge_created id=tx_9XyZ status=success
```

ashley-cs: Ugh. So no schema validation prevented it — create_charge accepted amount_cents and succeeded. Customer got billed.

liam-ops: Repro steps from my side: ran a local curl hitting the same resolver service, saw identical decision. Reproduced with a unit test that simulates ambiguous aliases.

matt-eng: Quick mitigation: disabled billing.create_charge in the router for proration intent (temporary) and queued a reversal for tx_9XyZ. Please confirm reversal and notify customer if refund goes through.

ashley-cs: Confirmed reversal queued. Customer notified.

matt-eng: Root cause: alias overlap + small scoring delta because of historical usage weight. Two fixes proposed: (1) require explicit namespace prefix for billing-critical tools when multiple candidates exist, (2) raise lexical penalty for antonyms (charge vs credit) in the similarity scorer, (3) add a schema-level safety check that refuses to call a tool if the tool's primary schema doesn't semantically match intent (e.g., credit vs debit).

ev an-support: (typo) evan-support: Sounds good — which one can we push quickly?

matt-eng: Short term: deploy change to router config to mark billing.create_charge as low-priority for intents containing "prorate" or "credit". Medium term: add a hard validation hook that compares intent labels -> tool financial direction. I'll open an ENG-RUNTIME ticket.

liam-ops: Repro notes attached — curl used: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://router.internal/v1/resolve \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_KEY" \
 -d '{"input":"swap startup->pro prorate true","context":{"customer_id":"cus_ABC123"}}'
```
Response shows selected_tool: billing.create_charge and args.amount_cents: 12000.

tool-router-bot: Escalation filed to eng-runtime: ENG-9876. Priority: P1 (billing user impact).

ashley-cs: Customer follow-up: thank you for quick response, will wait for refund confirmation.

matt-eng: I'll own the ENG-9876 PR. Plan: config change today, safety hook next week. Will post diffs and canary notes. :thumbsup:

liam-ops: Added a unit test and a canary to block create_charge for intents containing ["prorate","refund","credit"] until scoring changes land.

evan-support: Closing loop — refund issued, customer notified, tracking in INC-4321. Good catch everyone. :tada:
